subject.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens

question: After resolving conflicts, should OpenClaw preserve policy-filtered MCP/LSP runtime selector tokens in child inherited allowlists as this PR does, or move the fix closer to runtime materialization?
rationale: The PR fixes a real missing-tool path, but the permanent boundary controls child-session authorization and overlaps newer policy code that is not represented in the branch head.

options.title: Refresh And Confirm Policy Parity
options.body: Resolve conflicts, keep the selector-preservation approach, and require owner review that the refreshed merge filters selectors through the same effective policy intersection as concrete tools.

options.title: Accept After Refresh
options.body: Maintainers may land the refreshed branch if they judge the supplied proof and tests sufficient for this authorization boundary.

options.title: Replace Near Runtime Materialization
options.body: If owner review finds inherited selector preservation is the wrong boundary, pause this branch and replace it with a narrower fix at MCP/LSP runtime construction.

recommendation.title: Refresh And Confirm Policy Parity
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts, keep the selector-preservation approach, and require owner review that the refreshed merge filters selectors through the same effective policy intersection as concrete tools.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent declared allowlist work overlaps the current conflict area and the policy semantics this PR must preserve.
